title: Wellness Ranch | On-Page SEO Strategy
text:
The Wellness Ranch On-Page SEO Strategy project demonstrates the application of search engine optimization, digital marketing research, and website performance analysis to a nonprofit organization.
Wellness Ranch Equine Assisted Therapy is a nonprofit organization based in Rancho Cucamonga, California, providing equine-assisted therapeutic services.
The project focused on developing a comprehensive SEO strategy to improve website discoverability, strengthen organic search visibility, and connect prospective clients with relevant therapeutic resources.






NoteIndividual Contribution



I served as the On-Page SEO Team Lead, contributing to keyword research, website auditing, metadata optimization, internal linking, structured data planning, and strategic performance recommendations.

title: Wellness Ranch | On-Page SEO Strategy
text:
Business Problem
Nonprofit organizations frequently face challenges competing for online visibility due to limited marketing resources, technical website constraints, and competition from established service providers.
For Wellness Ranch, improving organic search visibility represents an opportunity to increase awareness of equine-assisted therapy and connect with individuals searching for mental health and therapeutic services.
The project addressed the following strategic challenges:

Limited non-branded keyword visibility.
Website crawlability and indexing concerns.
Opportunities to improve metadata and content structure.
Limited organic search measurement capabilities.
Opportunities to strengthen internal linking.
Website accessibility and technical performance.

title: Google Analytics 4 Micro Application
text:
Google Analytics 4 Measurement Framework

Event-Based Measurement
Unlike traditional session-based analytics models, Google Analytics 4 uses an event-based measurement framework.
Website and application interactions are captured as events, allowing marketers to examine user behavior across digital environments.
Examples of measurable events include:

Page views
Session starts
User engagement
Product views
Add-to-cart interactions
Purchases
Form submissions

Events can be designated as key events when they represent actions important to business objectives.


User and Session Dimensions
GA4 distinguishes between user-scoped, session-scoped, and event-scoped information.
Understanding these distinctions is important when interpreting acquisition and marketing performance reports.







Dimension
Analytical application




First user source
Identifies the source associated with initial user acquisition.


Session source
Identifies the source associated with a session.


Session medium
Describes the marketing medium associated with a session.


Default channel group
Organizes traffic into standardized marketing channels.


Event name
Identifies a specific recorded interaction.

title: Designing a Professional Quarto Website
text:
Understanding CSS and SCSS

What is CSS?
Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) is a stylesheet language used to control the presentation of HTML documents. CSS allows developers to customize typography, colors, spacing, borders, positioning, and responsive layouts without changing the underlying content.


What is SCSS?
SCSS is an extension of CSS that introduces additional programming features, including variables, nesting, reusable rules, and mixins.
Quarto compiles SCSS into standard CSS and integrates custom themes with the Bootstrap framework.

text:
Integrating Stylesheets with Quarto

Website Configuration
The _quarto.yml configuration file connects the website to its custom SCSS theme and CSS stylesheet.
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, theme.scss]
    css: styles.css


Dashboard Configuration
The dashboard uses its own format configuration to apply the same design system.
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: [cosmo, theme.scss]
    css: styles.css
    scrolling: true
    embed-resources: false
Using both configurations helps maintain a consistent visual identity between standard website pages and interactive dashboards.

title: Professional Project Portfolio
text:
Understanding Quarto Listings

What are Quarto Listings?
Quarto Listings provide an automated approach to organizing and displaying website content based on document metadata.
Rather than manually updating a portfolio whenever a new project is completed, listings allow Quarto to dynamically generate a collection of project entries during the rendering process.
This functionality is particularly useful for:

Professional portfolios
Academic research websites
Marketing analytics projects
Blogs and publications
Data science case studies
Project documentation



Types of Listings
Quarto supports several listing formats depending on the intended presentation and audience.








Listing type
Description
Recommended application




Default
Vertically organized content
Blogs and articles


Grid
Card-based visual presentation
Professional portfolios


Table
Structured rows and columns
Research and project directories



This portfolio uses the grid format to create a structured and visually accessible presentation of professional projects.

title: Professional Project Portfolio
text:
Implementing Quarto Listings

Project Organization
Each project is maintained as an individual Quarto document within a dedicated projects directory.
M10/
├── _quarto.yml
├── index.qmd
├── cep.qmd
├── dashboard.qmd
├── customization.qmd
├── listings.qmd
├── theme.scss
├── styles.css
└── projects/
    └── Individual project documents (.qmd)
This structure separates website navigation, visual customization, analytical dashboards, and individual project content.


Document Metadata
Each project document contains a YAML header that defines its title, description, and relevant categories.
For example:
---
title: "Credit Union Customer Insights"
description: "An interactive dashboard examining customer satisfaction and financial product awareness."
categories:
  - Marketing Analytics
  - Customer Insights
  - Data Visualization
---
Quarto extracts this metadata and uses it to automatically populate the portfolio listing.


Listing Configuration
The following YAML configuration demonstrates how a grid-based listing can be implemented.
listing:
  id: portfolio-projects
  contents: projects
  type: grid
  grid-columns: 2
  categories: true
  sort-ui: true
  filter-ui: true
  sort: "title asc"
  fields: [title, description, categories]



Configuration
Function




id
Identifies the listing placement


contents
Specifies the source directory


type
Determines the presentation format


grid-columns
Sets the number of grid columns


categories
Enables category-based navigation


sort-ui
Enables interactive sorting


filter-ui
Enables search functionality


sort
Defines the initial sorting order


fields
Determines the displayed metadata

Customer relationship management platforms provide organizations with opportunities to improve customer relationships, operational efficiency, and sales performance.
However, the effectiveness of CRM technology depends on consistent adoption, meaningful user engagement, and integration into organizational workflows.
Understanding adoption patterns and potential barriers can help organizations identify opportunities to improve technology utilization and employee engagement.

title: Salesforce CRM Adoption Research
text:
Theoretical Research Framework

Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)
The Technology Acceptance Model examines how perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use influence attitudes toward technology and behavioral intentions.
Within the context of Salesforce adoption, TAM provides a framework for investigating whether users perceive the platform as beneficial to their responsibilities and sufficiently accessible to incorporate into their workflows.


Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT)
UTAUT extends technology acceptance research by examining four central constructs:

Performance expectancy
Effort expectancy
Social influence
Facilitating conditions

These constructs provide a broader perspective for understanding how individual perceptions and organizational conditions may influence Salesforce adoption.


Framework Comparison








Dimension
TAM
UTAUT




Primary focus
Individual technology acceptance
Individual and organizational adoption


Key constructs
Usefulness and ease of use

Strength
Parsimonious and interpretable
Broader explanatory framework


Limitation
Limited organizational context
Greater measurement complexity


CRM application
Understanding user perceptions
Examining adoption within organizational environments



These frameworks represent theoretical approaches for investigating adoption. Their empirical evaluation depends on the availability of appropriate measurements.

title: Salesforce CRM Adoption Research
text:
Analytical Methodology
The proposed analytical workflow consists of the following stages:

1. Research and Literature Review
Evaluate established academic research concerning CRM adoption, technology acceptance, employee engagement, and organizational behavior.


2. Data Preparation
Prepare available Salesforce CRM records for analysis through data cleaning, variable assessment, missing-value evaluation, and appropriate aggregation.


3. Exploratory Data Analysis
Examine observable patterns in platform activity, user engagement, and CRM utilization.


4. Adoption and Engagement Analysis
Develop appropriate behavioral indicators to assess differences in Salesforce usage and identify potential engagement patterns.


5. User Segmentation
Explore opportunities to segment users based on observable engagement characteristics and available organizational information.


6. Managerial Recommendations
Translate supported analytical findings into practical recommendations for improving CRM engagement and technology utilization.
